decisions.rationale: dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 10760, so no exact-duplicate removal is required.
id has distinct_count 10760 equal to dataset.row_count 10760 with null_rate 0.0, making it a reliable single-column grain for one row per runway.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all marked is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning, so they are dropped.

length_ft, width_ft, le_elevation_ft, he_elevation_ft, le_displaced_threshold_ft, and he_displaced_threshold_ft show only integral sample values despite landing as DECIMAL(38,9), so they are cast to INTEGER.
lighted and closed each have distinct_values [0.0, 1.0] with null_rate 0.0, so they are cast from DECIMAL to BOOLEAN.
le_latitude_deg, le_longitude_deg, he_latitude_deg, he_longitude_deg samples show 6-decimal precision within standard lat/long ranges, so they are narrowed from DECIMAL(38,9) to DECIMAL(9,6).

le_displaced_threshold_ft (null_rate 0.884201) and he_displaced_threshold_ft (null_rate 0.899907) are missing for the large majority of runways since most runway ends have no displaced threshold, so both are retained as nullable rather than dropped or imputed.

le_latitude_deg/le_longitude_deg/he_latitude_deg/he_longitude_deg (~0.22 null_rate), le_elevation_ft/he_elevation_ft (~0.276 null_rate), and le_heading_degt/he_heading_degt (~0.227 null_rate) are all sparsely populated but retained as nullable since geospatial detail is simply unrecorded for many runways.

purpose: This table provides a cleaned, one-row-per-runway view of OurAirports runway infrastructure data, including dimensions, surface, lighting/closure status, and each runway end's identifier, coordinates, elevation, heading, and displaced threshold, to feed downstream airport infrastructure and geospatial analyses.
usage: Join on id as the unique runway key or on airport_ref/airport_ident to associate runways with airports; consumers must handle null latitude/longitude/elevation/heading fields (~22-28% missing) and especially the displaced threshold fields, which are null for the large majority of rows (~88-90%) since most runway ends lack a displaced threshold. Use the lighted and closed boolean flags directly for filtering active, lit runways.
limitations: Cleanup did not resolve the unstandardized surface vocabulary (239 distinct free-text values with 2.3% nulls); le_ident and he_ident retain odd placeholder values like '.' and '-' as seen in bronze samples; geographic and physical fields (lat/long, elevation, heading, displaced threshold) retain substantial null rates (22%-90%) because the source data itself is incomplete, and no duplicate rows were found (duplicate_row_rate 0.0) so no dedupe logic was applied.
